source: Frank W. Gould (1975), The Grasses of Texas, Elymus virginicus, printed p. 166
source_material: Owner-supplied readable photograph of printed p. 166; page image is not republished.
scope: Character options and exact-species evidence only; preserve all 169 profiles, admissions, source alternatives, photographs and annotations.

option.label: Glume bases bow outward and lack veins
option.detail: Inspect the BASE of each outer glume: it bows away from the spikelet. Veins on the upper glume body do not imply veins continue through its base.

option.label: Firm, yellowish glumes
option.detail: Check mature outer glumes for a hardened texture and pale yellowish color; color alone does not establish identity.

option.label: Strongly veined glume body
option.detail: Trace the prominent veins on the glume BODY. This does not specify a vein count or claim that the base is veined.

option.label: Glume apex somewhat curved
option.detail: Examine the top of the outer glume, separately from the awn and the basal bow. This feature is variable.

option.label: Glume tapers into a straight awn
option.detail: Trace this awn to an OUTER GLUME, not a lemma. Its length may be shorter or longer than the glume body.

option.label: Stiffly upright spike
option.detail: Check the whole unbranched flowering spike. An erect flowering head is separate from an erect or basally decumbent culm.

option.label: Spike partly enclosed by upper leaf sheath
option.detail: Follow the upper leaf sheath to see whether it still surrounds the base of the attached spike. Often present, not obligatory.

option.label: Sparse stiff hairs on lemma
option.detail: Inspect a true lemma for scattered stiff hairs. Sparse hirsute hairs do not require a conspicuously fuzzy lemma.

option.label: Lemma awn straight or slightly curved
option.detail: Trace the awn to its lemma. Gould gives 5–25 mm; compare its straight or weakly curved shape without assuming an age-related bend.

option.label: Ligule top cut straight across (truncate)
option.detail: Inspect the overall top outline of the tiny inner membrane. A truncate outline does not prove its edge lacks fine teeth or cilia.

option.label: Sheath without hairs
option.detail: Inspect the sheath around the stem, separately from the blade and collar. A source may allow hairy variants; this observation never proves another variant absent.

option.label: Leaf blade without hairs
option.detail: Use magnification on the blade faces; hairless does not necessarily mean free of rough projections.

option.label: Leaf blade rough (scabrous)
option.detail: Check the blade SURFACE, not just its edge. Minute rough projections and fine hairs are different and can occur variably.

evidence.note: Tufted culms stand erect or lie low at the base before rising. This does not make the flowering spike nodding. Earlier H&L geniculate records remain as supplementary variation.

evidence.note: Outer glumes have strongly veined bodies, a hardened yellowish texture, and outward-bowed bases without veins. Their apex is often somewhat curved and narrows to a straight awn, whose length varies relative to the glume body. Do not infer an exact vein count.

evidence.note: Lemmas may lack hairs or have sparse stiff hairs. The sparse variant is distinct from the conspicuously hairy option; a hairless lemma is not necessarily polished or shiny.
